Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Nexus Energy Holdings Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. If you would like to register for a question, please press * then 1 on your touchtone phone. If you're using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Nexus Energy Holdings' Q3 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are John Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and Lisa Patel, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to John Reynolds.

John Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by strong operational performance in our generation fleet, continued growth in our renewable energy portfolio, effective cost management, and progress on our infrastructure investments.

Let me provide some more detail on these four key aspects. First, our strong operational performance has been bolstered by major advances in grid modernization and smart grid initiatives, which have enhanced reliability across our network. Second, we're seeing robust expansion in renewables, contributing to both regulated and merchant revenues. Third, disciplined cost controls have generated meaningful savings, particularly through demand response and outage reductions. Fourth, our infrastructure investments are fueling steady rate base expansion amid favorable regulatory outcomes.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Chen to discuss the financials.

Michael Chen: Thank you, John, and good morning, everyone. For the third quarter, we reported earnings per share of $0.98 and revenue of $3.25 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $750 million, primarily focused on grid modernization efforts, transmission and distribution upgrades, and renewable energy additions. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders.

To give you deeper insight into the drivers behind these results, let me expand on the key aspects John highlighted, starting with our grid modernization and smart grid initiatives—one of our highest-return growth areas. In this time of rapid electrification, rising renewables integration, and the need for resilience against severe weather, these investments are essential, transforming our efficiency, customer experience, and value creation for shareholders.

On the financial side, year-to-date, we've committed $450 million to grid modernization, accounting for 18% of our $2.5 billion total CapEx budget and marking a 25% increase from last year. This breaks down to $220 million for advanced metering infrastructure, $120 million for distribution automation, and $110 million for synchrophasor and sensor networks. Looking forward, we anticipate $1.2 billion in smart grid spending over the next three years, financed through rate base mechanisms in our state PUC filings—where we've achieved 85% approval on modernization riders—and low-cost debt at a blended 4.2% after-tax cost.

Progress-wise, we've upgraded 68% of our 45,000-mile distribution grid, completing full AMI rollout in our Northeast and Midwest areas, reaching 4.2 million customer endpoints. This surpasses our 2025 goal of 75% coverage, aided by collaborations with GE Vernova on Multilin relays and Siemens Energy's Spectrum Power DMS. Just in Q3, we installed 250,000 smart meters with a 98.5% success rate, enabling two-way communication that has yielded $28 million in annual savings from demand response.

Technologically, we're leveraging IIoT and edge computing across the board. Our DMS is integrated with OMS, powered by AI predictive analytics from Schneider Electric's EcoStruxure. We've installed over 5,000 PMUs and 12,000 IEDs on transmission lines, delivering sub-second grid visibility through our WAMS. These efforts cut our SAIDI by 22% year-over-year to 78 minutes, from 100, and SAIFI by 15% to 0.92 per customer—beating the NERC average of 1.1.

Tailoring by region, in the Northeast—serving 2.8 million customers amid PJM's queue constraints and 25 GW of renewables—we've emphasized DER integration. Our VPP pilot, with 15 MW of residential batteries via Sunrun, aggregates 8,000 behind-the-meter assets, dispatching 2.5 GWh in Q3 to reduce peaks and secure $4.2 million in PJM capacity payments, aligning with FERC Order 2222 and 40% RPS goals.

In the Southwest, dealing with hydro variability from droughts and data center surges from Microsoft and Google, we've spent $65 million on microgrid controllers and 5G FANs, achieving fault isolation in under 100 milliseconds for our 1.2 GW solar-plus-storage. For EVs, 1,200 Level 2 and 50 DC fast chargers at substations give us 12% market share, with $15 million in projected ancillary revenue by 2026 via our ApexGrid app.

Cybersecurity is paramount; we've implemented NERC CIP v6 segmentation, zero-trust from Palo Alto Networks, and quantum-resistant pilots per NIST. Our OT/IT integration using IEC 61850 GOOSE has lowered breach risk by 35%, per recent audits.

These moves create a positive feedback loop: reliability improvements lifted CSI to 92/100 from 84, reducing churn by 8% and easing rate approvals. Smart grid CapEx yields 12-15% IRR, from $75 million in avoided outages ($15,000/minute for industrials) and $40 million in asset optimization, like 20% longer transformer life via ML thermal models.

Ahead, this positions us for tailwinds like DOE's $10.5 billion GRIP—where we won $150 million for Texas projects—IRA's 30% ITC for storage, and FERC's DER NOPR. By 2027, smart grid should add 15% to regulated ROE uplift, aiming for 10.5% overall, while safeguarding our 50 GW portfolio amid 12% annual load growth from electrification.

Next, turning to rate base growth and the factors influencing it—the foundation of our earnings stability. This represents our net plant-in-service and eligible CWIP, on which regulators let us earn our authorized ROE, averaging 9.8% across six states.

At 2023 year-end, rate base was $28.4 billion, up 6.2% from $26.7 billion in 2022. Through Q3 2024, we've added $1.2 billion in new assets, pushing pro forma rate base to $29.1 billion—a 6.8% YoY rise. We're tracking toward 6.5% to 7.0% full-year growth, at the top of our 6-7% CAGR to 2028. AFUDC equity added 15 basis points from $850 million in CWIP.

Key drivers include our $12.5 billion five-year CapEx plan, approved or in process. Generation is 35%, or $4.4 billion, driven by clean transition: 450 MW solar in Texas via ERCOT, like the 250 MW Lone Star with First Solar modules eligible for IRA ITC transfers. BESS added 200 MW/800 MWh at Desert Peak, Arizona, paired with gas for ancillary services—accretive via formula rates.

T&D CapEx, 45% or $5.6 billion, leads: $450 million YTD in 345 kV transmission (15 miles in PJM for NERC risks) and $300 million in distribution hardening with 65% AMI penetration. In Southeast Georgia, data centers from Google/Microsoft bumped forecasts to 2.5% growth, approving $1.1 billion extra CapEx. In California CPUC, solar saturation slows to 4%, balanced by $800 million wildfire trackers.

Customer load rose 2.1% YTD, beating 1.8% forecast, from EV sales (8% new in Florida), industrial recovery. AI/data centers locked 1.2 GW new commitments in PJM/MISO, like peers Dominion or Entergy. Efficiency tempers to 1.5% long-term.

Headwinds: regulatory variability—Georgia's $450 million case seeks 10.35% ROE/52% equity, but faces scrutiny; 20-30 bps lag in formula states offset by Texas decoupling. Inflation hits 2-3% via A&G, transformers up 40%, but 85% plan has escalators. Debt costs up 50 bps to 6.2% WACC on 4.3% Treasuries.

For 7%+ post-2025: hybrid formulas in two states by 2026 like NextEra; $2 billion unregulated via Orsted JV for 600 MW Gulf offshore; Fluence/Tesla for 1.5 GWh storage clearing 95% PJM BRA at $270/MW-day; M&A like Texas bolt-on.

This supports $3.85-$4.00 2024 EPS and 6-8% long-term growth.

Now, our revenue breakdown by regulated and unregulated segments totaled $3.25 billion in Q3, up 8% from $3.0 billion last year. This underscores regulated stability with unregulated upside from spark spreads and renewables dispatch in PJM/ERCOT.

Regulated revenues were $2.1 billion, 65% of total, up 6% YoY. Covering T&D in six states—Northeast (4.2M customers PJM/ISO-NE), Texas ERCOT, Midwest MISO—growth came from 4% load rise (1,200 MW peak from data centers/industrials) and 5% above-normal heating degrees.

Rate wins: Pennsylvania settled 9.75% ROE/52.5% equity, $450 million revenue from $1.2 billion modernization CWIP (ADMS, 150k smart meters for DER). Texas URI rider: $220 million for resiliency, 500 MW Tesla pilots. AFUDC: $35 million from $2.8 billion 2024 regulated CapEx on T&D/FERC 881 incentives. Transmission up 12% to $620 million, PJM BASE at $270/MW-day—our 3.5 GW at 15% premium. EBITDA margins 28%, offset by digital twin O&M gains vs. 3% inflation.

Unregulated: $1.15 billion, 35%, up 12%. From 12 GW gas peakers/CCGTs and 5 GW renewables (offshore, solar, hydro) in CAISO/ERCOT/SPP. Heatwaves drove: $2.85/MMBtu Henry Hub, $45/MWh ERCOT spreads, 75% gas CF. Renewables 4.2 TWh, +18%, 450 MW new solar PPAs with Google/Microsoft, IRA PTCs.

1.2 GW Massachusetts offshore (GE Haliade-X) at 85% availability, $180 million fixed PPA. Hedged 85% 2024/70% 2025, collars for AI demand (15% ERCOT CAGR). ERCOT 45% unregulated (from 38%), $200/MWh peaks; PJM 30%; CAISO 15% via LCFS on 800 MW solar-storage.

60% of $5.5 billion 2024 CapEx to regulated (6-8% EPS), 40% unregulated ($1.1 billion for 1.2 GW hybrids, 90% PPAs). Balances 10.5% ROE with 12% IRR, FTRs/virts. 2025: regulated +7% riders/load, unregulated 15%+ IRA/tax equity.

Finally, a quick note on management's perspectives on industry trends and challenges. We're in a pivotal era: decarbonization acceleration, demand surge, regulatory/infrastructure hurdles. Renewables dominate—EIA: 32 GW solar +25% 2023, 8 GW wind +15%; BNEF: 95% new capacity to 2028, solar LCOE $24-36/MWh vs. CCGT.

Electrification booms: NREL data centers 15-20% demand by 2030 (Google/MSFT/Amazon); ERCOT +10% Q3 peak 85 GW. EVs to 40M/200-300 TWh; CHIPS reshoring. BESS surges: 60% queues CAISO/ERCOT, LFP 4-hour, Form iron-air 100-hour.

Challenges: supply chains—polysilicon +50% H1 2024, EPC +10-15%; gas volatility $2.50-$4/MMBtu LNG ramps. FERC 2023: 2,300 GW queues, 5-7 yr delays; state mandates amid coal -10 GW, nuclear risks; PJM BRA $269/MW-day +300%. Aging infra: 42-yr avg lines, ERCOT 2.5 TWh curtailments.

We're countering with disciplined allocation, renewables hedging, supply diversification.

John Reynolds: Thank you, Michael. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: If you would like to ask a question, please press * then 1. Our first question comes from David Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Smith: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for grid modernization and smart grid initiatives going forward?

John Reynolds: Certainly, David. As Michael detailed extensively, our year-to-date $450 million investment is scaling to $1.2 billion over three years, with strong ROI from reliability gains, DER integration, and regulatory support like GRIP funding. We've accelerated AMI and DMS rollouts, outperforming reliability benchmarks, and we're tailoring regionally for PJM queues and Southwest data centers. This de-risks our portfolio while capturing electrification upside.

Operator: Our next question comes from Julie Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Julie Chen: Thanks. What is your outlook for rate base growth?

Michael Chen: Great question, Julie. We're on pace for 6.5-7% growth this year to $29.1 billion pro forma, driven by our $12.5 billion CapEx plan—generation clean adds like Texas solar/BESS, T&D hardening. Load tailwinds from data centers/EVs support it, with mitigations for regulatory lag and inflation via formulas and escalators. Long-term, 6-7% CAGR to 2028, plus unregulated levers like storage JVs and M&A.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Robert Lee: How are you mitigating risks related to industry challenges like supply chains and interconnection delays?

Lisa Patel: Thanks, Robert. On supply chains, we're diversifying suppliers beyond China for polysilicon/modules, locking long-term contracts, and leveraging IRA domestics. For FERC 2023 queues, we're prioritizing brownfield upgrades and co-located storage to bypass long waits, while advocating in PJM/ERCOT for faster processes. Gas volatility? Hedging 85% exposure and flexible peakers. Overall, our balanced regulated/unregulated mix and CapEx discipline keep us resilient.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to John Reynolds for closing remarks.

John Reynolds: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the Q3 2024, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Nexus Energy Holdings for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Nexus Energy Holdings.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
